title: Fix cumulative metering time-splay after ledger replay
creator: Evan Patel
description: After an emergency ledger replay to repair a corrupted shard on 2026-02-18, downstream Console charts show a stretched and duplicated per-model cumulative usage curve (time-splay) that persists after backfill completes. This ticket tracks the investigation and remediation to ensure the cumulative ledger replay does not distort per-model daily aggregations, quota burn rate, or billing exports. Goals: 1) identify root cause in replay watermark handling, 2) implement idempotent replay markers and corrected watermark propagation, 3) backfill reconciliation script to normalize console curves without double-counting, and 4) add automated checks to prevent recurrence.
comments: 2026-02-20 - Evan Patel: Ticket created after on-call flagged inconsistent cumulative curves in Console top-models. Initial hypothesis: replayed events retained original event_time but were re-ingested without replay markers, causing stitcher to include them twice across adjacent windows.

2026-02-22 - Sofia Ortega: Pulled sample event batches from blob store for Tenant: acme-inc. Observed duplicated token counts spanning two adjacent hourly buckets; the replay process used sequence_id reset which prevented stream de-duplication. Added reproducer script: tools/repro/replay_time_splay.py (internal).

2026-02-25 - Marcus Li (infra): Identified that shard-watermark persisted pre-replay timestamps; streaming stitcher merges by event_time only, so late replayed rows fall into older buckets but also remained in transient hot-cache leading to cumulative double-counts. Opened infra follow-up ENG-70123 for shard watermark progression fixes.

2026-03-01 - Sofia Ortega: Implemented prototype guard: attach replay_id metadata to re-ingested rows and skip rows where replay_id == current_replay during rollup. Benchmarked on staging with 3 tenants. Results: duplicate spikes eliminated but introduced increased window-latency for a subset of streaming aggregates. Trade-off: small increase in aggregation lag vs correctness.

2026-03-04 - Evan Patel: RFC posted in Confluence: 'Replay-safe rollup markers and idempotent ledger reingest' with design for replay tombstones and watermark revision. Link: https://confluence.company.internal/display/BILL/Replay+Safe+Rollup+Markers

2026-03-08 - Sofia Ortega: Submitted PR to repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing-rollup/pull/482 (WIP) implementing replay_id propagation and dedupe in the aggregator. Added unit tests and a tuning flag (AGG_REPLAY_DEDUPE=true) to gate rollout.

2026-03-10 - QA: Ran end-to-end backfill on staging tenant 'sandbox-001' with 14 days of synthetic replays. Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/usage/console-per-model?orgId=1&var-tenant=sandbox-001 shows normalized cumulative lines post-patch. Leaving elevated monitoring for 72h.

2026-03-12 - Sofia Ortega: Plan for production rollout: 1) enable AGG_REPLAY_DEDUPE on a canary shard (region-us-east-1) for low-risk tenants; 2) run normalization backfill job with idempotent transform (jobs/normalize_cumulative_backfill.sh) to reconcile pre-patch days; 3) monitor per-model diffs and billing export checks for mismatches. Scheduling rollout window 2026-03-16 02:00-05:00 UTC.
2026-03-12 - Evan Patel: Added dependency check: must wait for ENG-174561 (epoched-ingest-normalizer) to finish final verification before running customer-facing billing export normalization.
